# Citeswitcher

For simple collaboration in academic writing. Cite papers as PMID, DOI, bib reference, or whole citation, and citeswitcher will find them, make a common bib file for you, and convert them all to the format of your choice.

# TL;DR

`python fixcitations.py sup-files/test.md`

You can cite papers in a plain text document like this [PMID: 24465370] or like this [https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0081229] or [DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0081229] or (if you share a .bib file) like this [@HallNetworkAnalysisReveals2014] or (if you really need to) like this [Hall, David P., Ian J. C. MacCormick, Alex T. Phythian-Adams, Nina M. Rzechorzek, David Hope-Jones, Sorrel Cosens, Stewart Jackson, et al. “Network Analysis Reveals Distinct Clinical Syndromes Underlying Acute Mountain Sickness.” PLoS ONE 9, no. 1 (January 22, 2014): e81229].

Citeswitcher will find these and format them properly as citations in the chosen output format.

# Requirements

## OS
- works on all linux and mac systems tested so far
- not tested on windows

## Essential

For basic function of fixcitations.py:

- python 3
- pyparsing 2.4.7
- requests-2.24.0
- biopython
- oyaml
- bibtexparser is also required but it is included in this git repository (because I was concerned that it may not be well maintained)

To install these:
pip install pyparsing
pip install requests
pip install biopython
pip install oyaml

## Optional additional requirements

Once you have the above installed, you're good to go. Additional dependencies for extra functions are listed at the end.

# Installation

Download or clone the git repository into a folder on your hard disk. Then run the scripts using python from the command line.
To make it easier to use, I use the unix `alias` command in my `~/.bash_profile` to automatically map common commands, like this:

`alias fix="/miniconda3/envs/thisenv/bin/python <full-path-to-git-repository>/citeswitcher/fixcitations.py"`

## Config

Edit the `config.json` file to include your own paths before running. Key elements:

- email: required for using the Pubmed API - enter your own email address here.
- filepaths: these need to be on you computer somewhere.

# Use

## fixcitations.py

Switch citation formats, find missing citations online, and keep local/global bib files synchronized.

### Input files

Required:

- a `.md`, `.qmd`, `.tex`, `.txt`, or `.csv` document with references in square `[]`, curly `{}`, or round `()` brackets. Citations can be PMIDs, DOIs, bibtex refs, or whole references.

Optional:

- *bib file*.
	A local bibtex file to use (`-b/--bibfile`). If not specified, local bibliography selection priority is:
    1) `-b/--bibfile`
    2) YAML `bibliography` entries (in discovered order)
    3) `cs.bib` in the source folder
    4) any other `.bib` in the source folder (alphabetical)
    5) fallback create `_bib/cs.bib`
- *global bib file*.
	Specify a global bibtex file (`-gb/--globalbibfile`) used as the wider citation source.
- *yaml file*.
	You can pass `-y/--yaml` to add a specific YAML source file. YAML is discovered in this order:
    1) in-file YAML front matter
    2) `<filestem>.yaml`
    3) `<filestem>.yml`
    4) `_quarto.yml` in current folder, parent, then grandparent
    5) explicit `-y/--yaml` path (if provided)
    The script reads `bibliography` from these sources and writes `bibliography` / `csl` updates back to the most appropriate existing YAML target.
- *csl file*.
	You can specify `csl` in YAML. If no `csl` exists anywhere, `minimal.csl` is copied next to the chosen local bibliography and YAML is updated automatically.

#### Extra functions

- *replace.json file*.
	A file called `replace.json` will be read as a dictionary of text strings to find:replace. If you just create this file and leave it in the same directory as the input file, it will be read. An alternative is to specify text to be replaced in a YAML dict format.

- files to include.

The default (in `config.json`) or specified .bib file will be searched for the relevant citations.
Citations will be replaced with a citaion in either .md or .tex or PMID format.

Any citations not found in the .bib files will be downloaded from pubmed and added to the supplementary.bib file

### Output files

- Main output document with transformed citations:
  - overwrite original by default
  - write sidecar output when `-s/--safemode` is used (e.g. `.citemd.` / `.citetex.` / `.citepmid.` in filename)
- Local bibliography output (`.bib`) containing merged local+newly-cited entries.

## Options

| arg | long arg| action|
|----|--------------|---------------------------|
| *(positional)* | `filepath_positional` | input file path (equivalent to `-f`) |
| -f | --filepath | input file path |
| -gb | --globalbibfile | global bibtex file |
| -b | --bibfile | bibfile |
| -y | --yaml | specify an additional YAML file to search |
| -o | --outputstyle | choices=md,markdown,tex,latex,pubmed,pmid; output references format |
| -s | --safemode | write sidecar output instead of overwriting input |
| -l | --localbibonly | use only local bib file |
| -w | --wholereference | try to match whole references. |
| -i | --propagateincludes | recursively fix citations in Quarto included documents using `{{< include ... >}}` |
| -flc | --force_lowercase_citations | force all citation references into lowercase |
| -v | --verbose | verbose logging |

### Propagate citations into Quarto includes (`-i/--propagateincludes`)

If your `.qmd`/`.md` file uses Quarto include shortcodes like:

`{{< include sections/methods.qmd >}}`

then running `fixcitations.py` on just the top-level file will *not* automatically edit the included files. Use `-i` (or `--propagateincludes`) to recursively open each included document and run the same citation-fix pass on it.

- Uses the **same chosen local bibliography** (the `cs.bib` selected for the original/top-level file, or the `-b/--bibfile` you passed).
- Uses the **same CLI options** you passed (output style, whole-reference matching, lowercase forcing, etc).
- Includes are resolved **relative to the file that contains the include**.
- Cycles are handled safely (each file is processed at most once).

Example:

`python fixcitations.py -f manuscript.qmd -o md -i`

## hackmd.py

Uses `wget` to download your **published** files from hackmd.io and runs fixcitations.py. This makes working collaboratively with hackmd very easy, but takes a bit of manual setup:

1. Specify the filepath to a directory (`hackmddir`) in `config.json`. This should be an empty directory.
2. *Within* your new `hackmddir`, create a folder with the exact name of your [hackmd.io](hackmd.io) username or group name.
3. Create a hackmd file and publish it. It's easier if you choose the url name for it, such as "mytestfile"
4. Create yet another folder with the same name as your hackmd file. So your directory structure would be like this:
```
- my_hackmd_dir
|	+-- my_username
|		+-- mytestfile

```
5. Run `python hackmd.py`

If this works, your file should download into the mytestfile directory, and you should see the following files:
```
- my_hackmd_dir
|	+-- my_username
|		+-- mytestfile
|			+-- mytestfile.md
|			+-- mytestfie.citemd.md
|			+-- mytestfie.citemd.pdf
|			+-- mytestfie.citemd.docx
|			+-- mytestfie.citemd.html
```

hackmd.py - download hackmd files either by combining elements from a directory tree or a single file, then run fixcitations.py

# Additional utilities

The following additional scripts are included to provide some useful functions with varying levels of documentation:
- *include.py* - include files recursively according to a variety of syntaxes
- *put_pmid_in_bibtex.py* - search for PMIDs for every element in a .bib file. Designed to run as a cron job to keep your bib file up to date.
- *abbreviation_finder.py* - print abbreviations in a document (so that you can explain them)
- *wordcount.py* - function unknown at this time
- *svg2pdf.py* - batch convert a directory (-d) or file (-f) using cairosvg, which seems to perform better than imagemagick.
- *format_author_list.py* - this is a work in progress but it is intended to create author lists in a variety of formats from a spreadsheet in xlsx or csv format

# Intended use:
- Feed in a .md or .tex document
- references in square [] or curly {} brackets will be searched for:
-- PMID
-- doi
-- bibtext
-- whole ciation

### For making Gantt, flowcharts etc

- mermaids.cli (https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli)
Mermaids is a bit of a hassle to install and needs to be in you PATH variable for this to work. But if it is in there, you can use the -pm option to call mermaids and automatically generate nice figures.

This installation procedure worked for me on a mac:

#### Install node:
https://www.npmjs.com/get-npm
#### Install pandiff:
https://github.com/davidar/pandiff

#### Install mermaid:
`npm install mermaid.cli`
Test it: 
`./node_modules/.bin/mmdc -h`
Add mermaid to ~/.bash_profile:
export MERMAID_BIN=/Users/<username>/node_modules/.bin/mmdc
export PATH=$PATH:/Users/<username>/node_modules/.bin
~


# Flowchart

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    Start([Start]) --> ReadFiles[Read Input Files]
    ReadFiles --> |Text| ParseHeader[Parse YAML Header]
    ReadFiles --> |BibTeX| ReadBibs[Read Local & Global BibTeX]
    
    ReadBibs --> MergeBibs[Merge BibTeX Databases]
    MergeBibs --> HandleDuplicates[Handle Duplicate Entries]
    HandleDuplicates --> BuildDicts[Build Reference Dictionaries]
    
    ParseHeader --> ProcessCitations[Process Citations]
    BuildDicts --> ProcessCitations
    
    ProcessCitations --> |Mixed Citations| ExtractMixed[Extract Mixed Citations]
    ProcessCitations --> |LaTeX Citations| ExtractLatex[Extract LaTeX Citations]
    ProcessCitations --> |Word Citations| ExtractWord[Extract Word Citations]
    ProcessCitations --> |Whole References| ExtractWhole[Extract Whole References]
    
    ExtractMixed --> FindRefs[Find References]
    ExtractLatex --> FindRefs
    ExtractWord --> FindRefs
    ExtractWhole --> FindRefs
    
    FindRefs --> |Local DB| LocalLookup{In Local DB?}
    LocalLookup --> |Yes| FormatCitation[Format Citation]
    LocalLookup --> |No| GlobalLookup{In Global DB?}
    
    GlobalLookup --> |Yes| AddToLocal[Add to Local DB]
    GlobalLookup --> |No| PubMedSearch[Search PubMed]
    
    PubMedSearch --> |Found| AddToGlobal[Add to Global DB]
    PubMedSearch --> |Not Found| MarkMissing[Mark as Missing]
    
    AddToGlobal --> AddToLocal
    AddToLocal --> FormatCitation
    MarkMissing --> FormatCitation
    
    FormatCitation --> ReplaceText[Replace in Text]
    ReplaceText --> SaveFiles[Save Updated Files]
    
    SaveFiles --> End([End])

```
